chapter: Navy years and attitudes toward whites
title: Boot training at Great Lakes
summary: A country boy arrives in Chicago in a zoot suit without an overcoat; punishments in boot training and liberty in Boston.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah, okay, yeah, well I wound up with the GED. And, you know, first of all, I went to go into Great Lakes, Illinois, and I took this training, went up there, you know, that's what we didn't talk about, the little country boy, Shrewsbury, going up there. I went up there without an overcoat in December, Chicago, cold, froze to death. And I remember I had a zoot suit. You had a zoot suit?
Can you tell me what a zoot suit was?

Yeah, well, I don't know if you remember the Cab Calloway thing. It was the big hat with the feather in it and the long coat with the chad and the tight-legged pants. Well, I had a gray suit suit when I went in there. And I got to Chicago, and it was cold. And I didn't have no overcoat, because we didn't even need no overcoat down here. And, well, after a week or two, I think they made up the companies, and then we had three months of boot training. And I was punished twice, neither time seriously, in boot training. Excuse me. That's the coat coming up. Well, one time for making unnecessary noise in the bunk when the officer was coming through, and they made me get up. See, we had hammers. I had to get up and take my hammer, tie it up, and go stand out on it, and go march out in front of the barracks for an hour. And one other time there was this fellow who was from Tennessee. He thought he was a bully. He was a bully in the club. And they'd pick on him, and I'd just let him know I wasn't afraid of him, even though he was bigger than me. And he and I got into a scuffle, and so I was punished for that. But that's the only time. No, oh, one other time, the real serious time was, well, it was after boot training where they put me in a break over the weekend for leaving a work duty. I left the work duty. I left, we were supposed to leave at 12 o'clock, but I left at 11.30. And went to the barracks, slipped through the back, and got my shoes and my brother's shoes and shining because it was going on Liberty. And the officer today came, if I mean it. And that's the only time I had it. That's the only bad thing. In the three years I stayed in the service. That's all.
Where would y'all go on Liberty?
Okay. You were talking about Great Lakes, Illinois. Yeah.
Well, Great Lakes, Chicago, that's where we had the boot training. That's the beginning.
Did you go into Chicago? No, no.
That's boot training. So after Great Lakes, you all went to?
